BEST LINES (canvas, alpha 0.35)
- A dashed horizontal line at your deepest on this leg, 'deepest · 97 m', and a dashed vertical line at your farthest, 'farthest · 142 m'.
- Crossing one fires the beat 'NEW DEEPEST' or 'NEW FARTHEST' and the bell, once.
- From M8, a faint grey fossil of your last attempt on the leg.

END-SCREEN COUNT-UP (showMineEnd 29281)
- SPORED, or ISLAND on landfall, then '57 m down · 94 m east'.
- Lines count up over 1.2 s, each with a tick:
  - 'Reach 57 m + 94 m  +30 P'
  - 'Seams  +6 P  +12 Anthracite'
  - 'Island  +30 P'
  - 'Total  +66 P'
- Materials are always named.
- The P glyph is sized 0.95em; .ss-win-earned has no .ss-ri rule today (CSS 1760), which makes it 55-170 px.
- NEXT, first match wins:
  1. the best affordable rung, with an inline [Buy · 50 P];
  2. else the nearest one: 'Heat tolerance III · 30 Anthracite, you have 22 (found at 42-84 m)';
  3. else 'The island is 26 m past your farthest';
  4. else 'Your deepest is 4 m below this'.
- Buttons: [Descend] (primary) and [Store].
- A record adds the line 'Your farthest on Leg 3'.

BEATS
- Band: '42 m · ANTHRACITE · digs cost 4'. The price comes from mineGrowCost at that depth, so with tolerance it reads 'digs still cost 2'.
- Leg banner at every run start.
- 'LANDFALL' when the colony surfaces. The island hill blooms (startCelebration 'island', 33442) and the camera eases to it over 1.5 s.
- The kit buttons pulse while their threat is present.
- The price chip morphs into the FRUIT NOW pill with a countdown ring.
retention:
TOMORROW
1. The journey is unfinished, and every end screen names a near goal: 'island 26 m past your farthest', 'Heat III: 30 Anthracite, you have 22'. Closing the tab feels like pausing, not finishing.
2. The leg you failed yesterday is the same world today, fixed seed, with your farthest line in it and, from M8, your fossil. The retry is visible mastery, the way Trials ghosts and Souls bloodstains are, and failure reads as map knowledge.
3. Daily Dive (M10): one paid run a day on a shared UTC-date seed with a fixed standard kit, scored on best depth. It is local by default and online only once the owner has run the Supabase migration. A 60-second ritual.

WEEK ONE
- The journey is 26-40 runs (50-90 min), so 3-6 sessions, each with a 'first' (a band, a track, a leg modifier, an island).
- The Promised Land is a real ending with credits.
- Then New Journeys II-VIII: one cumulative rule each on fresh seeds, 30-45 min each with the kit.
- Each journey gives a Strain, a title badge and a 'fewest runs to the Promised Land' record; the strains shelf absorbs surplus P.
- A completionist has 4-7 hours of reasons.

WHY THESE. Each reuses the existing loop instead of adding a system (the owner's 'too complex' rule):
- legs reuse the map generator;
- lines and fossils are canvas polylines over it;
- New Journey is one knob per journey on the same leg table;
- the daily reuses the free descent;
- strains are a tint on the network renderer (25529).

DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT
- Energy timers, lives, or anything that blocks play. The owner: dying 'felt like you lost too much'.
- Login streaks that punish absence.
- Idle fruiting from islands: it rewards being away and floods P.
- Missions and quests: a second goal system on top of legs. Revisit if telemetry shows mid-journey churn.
- Prestige resets: they take the store away.
- Push notifications.
- Anything that needs the network to play.
fixesRequired: Dry-for-deep soft lock (36% of runs): mineCanGrow/mineFuelCheck (22694-22709) ask the shallowest strand. Ask the working front instead (one resting-view height around the focus strand), add a 1.6 s grace, then a 4 s FRUIT NOW countdown.
The only instruction is invisible on phones: .hint is display:none under 760 px (CSS ~693/~1011). Give the mine hint its own element plus a ghost-drag arrow.
A plain tap never digs, never commits an armed enzyme and never reframes, because endPointer returns at 36700. Mine taps should dig down, call mineArmedTap first, and double-tap to reframe.
Dev buttons are live on the public URL: 'Dev: maps' destroyed a run and '+10,000 spores' credits the mine wallet. Gate dev.inGameButtons and the store dev buttons behind #dev or ?dev.
The HUD pill is 423 px in a 390 px viewport and pushes the gear, the only End run, off screen. Use two rows under 430 px and a position:fixed gear.
'Replay tutorial' in the mine restarts the run with nothing banked. Hide it in the mine (settings 26396-26406, handlers 35971).
'Save & exit' deletes the run and its haul (onSaveExit 35976). Replace it with 'End descent', which banks through mineEndRun('abandon') and presentMineEnd.
'End run' prints 'The colony was eaten' because forceFruitAbandon sets died:true and the eaten branch at 33227 fires. Give each cause its own line.
The end-screen P icon renders 55-170 px because .ss-win-earned sizes .spore-ic but not .ss-ri (CSS 1760-1767). Size it at 0.95em.
Materials show as unlabelled dots on the HUD, store header and end screen, and seams look the same in every band. Print names (matName 28867) and tint seam art per material.
The SPORED wordmark clips both edges at 390 px. Clamp its width.
Run 1 cannot buy anything (3-18 P against a 10 P cheapest rung; 4 of 5 first visits dead). Set a minimum payout of 5 P and price Water I at 5 P.
Phosphorus comes only from the top 42 m; P per run is flat at 17 while 160 Anthracite piles up against 18 of demand. Add the reach payout (1 P per 5 m, down and east) and real material sinks.
Upgrades are too small to feel (Water +5 = 6% of the tank; 10 runs took start water from 84 to 94). Make Water +12 on a 60 start and use chunkier rungs.
The Mucus flask is one hit of three plus a 0.5 s stun and measured saving 0.1 water. In the mine one flask should kill every worm within 160 units.
One enzyme dose cannot cure a real breach (a 220-unit disc left 12 of 55 rotten). Cut the whole connected rotten component plus one segment of margin.
Worm breeding silently switches off after 4 chunks, because maxPopulation 16 counts the world against 4 worms per chunk. Cap attached worms per colony at 6 instead.
Worms are 10-16 px at the resting zoom and attach unseen from off screen. Draw them at 2.5x with a pulsing ring and a tether, and give the HUD chip an edge arrow.

Heat bypass: mineGrow prices the pressed strand while growDirected (~16290) falls through to any tip; measured, 137-142 m of growth for 2 water. Price at the parent that actually grows, and limit the fall-through to one grow reach.
A dig can 'succeed' 100+ m from where the player pressed, and the camera jumps there. Same fix; otherwise refuse with 'Solid rock that way'.
An infected ending under-reports depth (107 m reached, 99 m shown and recorded) because mineDepthReached skips rot. Keep a running maximum of clean depth in mineFrame.
The node cap of 6000 is shared (growth.maxNodes 2718); at the cap every dig says 'Solid rock' with water left. Give the mine its own cap of 9000 and a 'full' ending.
Ore yield also multiplies deep materials, its tile does not say so, and it is the dominant purchase. Remove the track and refund it.
Heat tolerance of +150 m deletes heat from a 168 m shaft halfway through the store. Use 21 m rungs, with the capstone (VI, Hematite) as the last rung.
The Water track is 57% of the shelf (1,849 P) for +5 a rung. Replace it with 6 rungs of +12 costing 509 P in total.
Store copy is wrong: the note always says '2 water a dig', the enzyme promises 'a small radius' (it is 220), and the flask never mentions the hits it needs. Rewrite the tiles.
No collection feedback on the map, and tapped pockets look untapped. Add floaters at the site and dim spent pockets.
Nothing happens at the 168 m floor and there is no goal once the record stops moving. Add the journey: legs, islands, the Promised Land.
Surface crust highway: row 0 is 5-7% solid, so 82 water crawls 168 m east. Wall the seams above each leg's trunk row in leg worlds.
The release zip prunes magnetite-c24 and garnet-c24 (make-web-zip.mjs 163-242), so bands 0 and 2 would ship with no rock and no collision. Keep every CONFIG.mine.bands[].assetsFrom folder.
itchzip-check (202) clicks #tsNewCamp/#tsNew, which the mine title no longer renders. Drive #tsNewMine through a descent, and add the check to run.mjs.
A dev-off build shows the campaign 'Level' card, and pauses, before every descent (pendingLevelIntro 35869-35904). Skip it for mine maps.

Collision is not ready when the map is: on a slow link solidAtWorld falls back to an empty cell.rock and 11 of 50 strands grew inside rock. Gate mineGrow on sub._rockSolidified, and preload the band folders at boot instead of the 71 card faces (_bootImgs 40486).
The HUD dig-cost chip reads the window.__game.mine.costHere() debug hook (27194). Call mineDigCost directly.
The load gate says 'CLICK' on phones, DIG takes about 6.9 s to become playable, and the title says 'start a new descent' after an exit. Say 'Tap to begin', be playable within 3 s, and fix the copy.
The title's Upgrades button appears only when P > 0, not when only materials are held (29889). Show it when any wallet is above zero.
mineBeat, mineZoom and mineClampZoom read CONFIG rather than state.config (37244-37251, 37143, 37161), so per-leg overrides would be ignored. Read state.config.
__game.mine.playSeed builds the world twice (35515). Start it once.
stampFood can return without pushing a pile, and 22123 then retags the previous pile with the wrong material. Check the return value before tagging.
About 7 O(nodes) passes run every frame, plus waterSourcesNear at O(25 x nodes). Cache extents incrementally in mineGrow and test pockets only against new nodes.
Closing the tab mid-run loses the haul. Bank on pagehide, or after 60 s hidden.
run_end telemetry carries no leg, distance east or duration. Use the existing carriers: detail 'J1L3', ms for duration, n for payout.
Bots: lib.cjs digAlong aims 130 units ahead whatever the grow reach, so the tier measurements undercount Grow strength. Set ahead to __game.mine.steps() x 3 x 25.5.
cutOrDeferred: CUT Ore yield track: it was dominant, doubled P and silently quadrupled deep materials. Income should come from progress (reach) rather than a separate multiplier. Refunded.
CUT Water pockets track: pocket value now scales by band, and the Water dowser sells pocket information instead of power. Refunded.
CUT Phosphorus compass: P seams are shallow, near the hill and plentiful, so a needle would sell almost nothing.
CUT a haul forfeit on infection, or freezing digging while infected (the breaker's 'give the deadline teeth'): it breaks the owner's full-payout premise. The deadline's teeth are the unspent tank.
CUT prestige or store resets for New Journey: the owner said losing progress felt bad. New Journey keeps the store and adds rules instead.
CUT idle fruiting from islands: it rewards absence rather than play, floods P, and adds a system.
CUT per-run modifiers picked before Descend: choosing is the drafting complexity the owner rejected. Leg modifiers are fixed per leg instead.
CUT mid-run resume: the owner's premise is no return trips and a descent in one sitting. 'End descent' and pagehide banking cover leaving.
CUT rock-eating as a general mechanic: rock is a wall. Only the bought, scarce Acid vial passes through it.

CUT a rock-edit vial that clips sprites and re-stamps the mask: that needs a new re-stamp-region function against the append-only mask. The vial lets the strand pass through rock instead, leaving the rock untouched.
DEFERRED three active missions: a second goal system on top of legs. Revisit if telemetry shows players quitting mid-journey.
DEFERRED secrets, motherlodes in dead ends, and a field journal: the owner said he will develop secrets later. Rich seams (1 in 4) are the only variable reward for now.

DEFERRED the online leaderboard: the Supabase host is unreachable from the container and needs an owner-run migration (level cap above 100, mode coercion at 14745). The Daily Dive is local first; online is optional and fails silently.
DEFERRED a fifth band or a deeper shaft per leg: that is an art-pipeline question. The four bands and 168 m carry 8 legs through trunk depth.
DEFERRED a mine-specific music track: an asset question (the itch zip has an entry cap). Synthesized SFX carry the feedback.

DEFERRED deleting the card-game residue (about 25% of the file): infectNetwork, excrete, amputateAt, waterSourcesNear and buildLevel are load-bearing, and deleting risks breakage for no player-visible gain. Only stop the card preload.
DEFERRED an achievements list: records, badges and strains do that job with less UI.
DEFERRED moving the mine to its own localStorage key: keep mycelium.progress.v2 with flag-guarded migrations; a key move is risk with no player value.

- The owner must run the SQL migration for the global board, and the anon key has no anti-cheat, so treat the board as casual.
- Fix playSeed's double start (35515) before any seeded daily.

premiseChanges: Water pockets pay by band (10/15/20/25) instead of the owner's flat +10. They stay a one-off burst, never an annuity. Evidence: a pocket sits at the end of an 8-12-cell spur, about 2.5 digs at the local price. At bare prices that is 5/10/20/40 water in bands 0-3, so a flat +10 is a net loss below 84 m. From leg 4 every route runs below 84 m, so pockets would stop being a decision in exactly the half of the game where the fuel clock is tightest.

Affordability asks the WORKING FRONT (the cheapest clean strand within one resting-view height of the focus strand), not the cheapest ground anywhere in the colony. A FRUIT NOW pill and a 4 s countdown after the existing grace end a stuck run. Evidence: the cheapest-ground rule (mineCheapestCost 22686) left 14 of 39 route-bot runs and 5 of 12 playtest runs live at 2-7 water against 4-16 a dig, for 30-60 s with nothing on screen affordable. The 'crawl sideways up top' recovery it was written for never happened in 51 runs. The only exits were a worm, the rot, or a gear menu the HUD had pushed off screen. Heat stays priced and never enforced, and any dig the game allows still succeeds.

scores.strengths: Best first-minute and moment-to-moment spec of the three. The first visit skips the title, so the tap-to-dig target is 1.5 s against 6.9 s today, which is the biggest single portal-retention win on the table. It adds a canvas ghost finger, a #minehint element of its own, tap-to-dig-down, and a dead-end nudge for runs 1-5. The end screen counts up the payout by source, shows one next-goal card with an inline Buy, and makes Descend the primary button (one tap to the next run). The juice list is complete and testable (__sfx.counts, floaters at the site, drained pockets, haptics, the price chip pulse). The store reveal shows at most 5 tiles before run 5. Milestones are in the right order (unblock and trust the tests first, then the first minute, economy, juice and threats, and the generator work last) and their acceptance tests are concrete, with line numbers. It changes no premise. The acid vial passes through rock and leaves the collision mask alone, which is the low-risk version. Compass chunks are generated lazily in idle time. Heat tolerance is capped at +36 m, so heat never disappears.
scores.weaknesses: The island is a SURFACE target. The economy agent measured the crust at 5-7% solid (82 water crawls 168 m east), so legs 1-4 become a flat drag-right crawl in which depth has nothing to do with the goal. The 'dive run vs east run' split then ends up as two half-games, and it only starts to bite at leg 5 through a seal modifier. Material sinks are thin (40 Anthracite, 32 Garnet, 39 Hematite of demand), so the 160-Anthracite pile-up returns by run 12-14. The escalating reach table [6,4,3,2] is harder to read than a flat rate. It carries extra systems that cut against 'few systems, each deep': offline island fruiting, a daily streak that pays +3 P a day, a colour shelf from leg 5, a core bonus and a first-descent floor. The lateral seam-to-seam repair in every chunk between home and island is real generator risk. The daily runs on the player's own loadout, so scores cannot be compared and the daily can be farmed.

scores.strengths: The most coherent design. It sets an explicit budget of five systems and makes every wrapper reuse them. The leg target is the island's TAPROOT, a glowing knot at depth under the east island. That fuses the two axes into every run: you must go down AND right, you meet the bands' materials and threats on the way, and the compass has one point to name through rock. It avoids the crust-highway problem and any climb back to the surface, so there are no return trips. Journey-1 seeds are curated by a legprobe from 50 candidates, and the generator change is limited to the island chunk with a hash-seeded rng. That is the lowest-risk route to guaranteed reachability, with no corridor. Other strong pieces: a dig that occupies no new cell is refunded, which directly fixes the naive player burning 44-60 water; one enzyme dose cuts the whole connected rotten component; strictTip closes the heat bypass; the heat cap is +56 m; there is a 'no material balance above 3x its remaining demand' rule; and each leg has one named rule that teaches one system. It rejects offline income, streak loot and cosmetic shops.
scores.weaknesses: Ten legs, 70-90 runs and 3-5 h, with late legs targeting 6-15 retries of one fixed map, is a grind risk for portal players. Multi-part prices ('110+10A') mean rewriting costParts across 5 call sites and add a double gate that is harder to read on a phone tile. The acid dissolves rock by editing _fineSolid and _coarseCover and re-applying holes after every restamp, which fights the append-only mask. The title and banner give away the island's exact east distance and depth ('170 m east, 50 m down') while the island compass is supposed to sell that precision. The end screen has a single 'To the store' button, costing an extra tap on every run. startWater is cut to 64 as a fixed number, which moves every fuel assertion before anything is measured. The taproot is a premise interpretation that needs the owner's sign-off. Its economy is less modelled than the economy proposal's.

scores.strengths: The most rigorous numbers. Route costs are measured (13/11/10/8 digs per band; 6 digs per chunk on the crust against about 9 at depth), there is a committed career model with a table of how results change with human overhead (1.8x to 3.0x), and it gives a usable tuning rule (price about 1-2 runs of income at that leg; every leg reachable at 70% or less of supply). It found the crust highway. It guarantees the run-1 purchase by construction (minimum payout 5 P = Water I at 5 P). The reach formula is the most legible ('1 P per 5 m, down or east', running maxima, never less than 5). FRUIT NOW shows what will bank ('+23 P'). It banks the run on pagehide or when the tab is hidden, so closing the tab never loses the haul. One deep seam in 4 is rich and pays x3, a cheap variable reward. It uses a separate rng stream so pinned seeds do not move. Its 'each band's material keys the next leg' chain is tight.
scores.weaknesses: The layout fights the owner. Forced rock walls run from the surface down to trunkRow-3 at every chunk seam, and a forced-open trunk row with repair is a reserved corridor in all but name, which the owner rejected twice. It also means a visible structural slab every 24 columns and the heaviest generator change of the three. Every leg has the same shape (down, along the trunk, back UP the island head), so the maze choice collapses into one highway, and the climb is priced at depth (bare leg 8 costs 2,250 water), which amounts to a return trip. Heat VI moves the first line to 168 m, deleting heat exactly at the finale; the breaker flagged this as a defect. Band-scaled pockets (10/15/20/25) change an owner number on the strength of a model, not a finding. Generating the whole leg eagerly at Descend (about 14 chunks, a long task of up to 600 ms) is a phone perf and memory risk. The banner gives away the island distance and trunk depth, undercutting the compass. A 26-40 run journey may end within an hour.

bestIdeasToGraft: SOFT-LOCK FIX, flagged to the owner as the ONE justified premise amendment (36% of runs are measured stuck), from all three plus economy's pill copy. When water < costHere (the number the price chip shows, at the focus strand), the chip becomes a FRUIT NOW pill showing what will bank ('FRUIT NOW · +23 P'), with a 5 s countdown ring. It starts only after the last reveal finishes and pauses while a menu is open. Any successful dig or any water gained cancels it. At zero the run auto-fruits with cause 'dry'.

LEG TARGET = the island's TAPROOT (craft): a canvas-drawn glowing knot in a carved chamber under the east island, at a depth that grows each leg. It counts as reached when a clean node is within about 1.5 cells. The celebration pulses filaments up to the island hill, which fruits, and the next leg starts from that island as the new west hill. The owner must confirm this as the reading of 'reach one, resurface and spore'. It removes the crust-highway crawl and any climb back up.

REACHABILITY WITHOUT CORRIDORS (craft): Journey-1 seeds are curated offline by a legprobe that requires the fine-mask flood to reach the taproot and a shortest path of 1.3-2.0x the straight line. The generator change is limited to the island chunk (chamber carve plus flood-and-repair on a hash-seeded rng). Journey 2+ seeds come from an offline-probed table. The 'free' #mine,<seed> layout stays byte-identical for the 190 mine-check assertions and for the daily.

ESCALATION TABLE, hand-authored, 8 legs, with one named rule per leg using existing knobs only (threatBands, reservoirsPerBand, heat.safeDepth, richness). Journey legs also raise the shallow-band gallery seal chance (retention's leg-5 idea, applied from leg 2-3) so the cheapest route to the taproot runs diagonally through the maze. Measure that with the legprobe; never use painted walls. Band 1 stays threat-free and nothing respawns.

PACING TARGETS: the first island by run 3-5 (minutes 5-8), 2-8 runs per leg, no leg needing more than 10, and the Promised Land in about 35-60 runs. That is retention's middle ground between craft's 70-90 and economy's 26-40.

REACH PAYOUT (economy's formula, retention's juice): +1 P per 5 m of running-maximum clean depth, plus +1 P per 5 m of running-maximum east on legs, never less than 5 P. It ticks live in the HUD with a '+1 P' pop at the tip, and it is paid and recorded from running maxima so rot never erases progress (the 107 m shown as 99 m bug).

RUN 1 ALWAYS BUYS, BY CONSTRUCTION (economy): the cheapest first rung (Water I) costs exactly the minimum payout (5 P). The first store shows exactly two tiles, Water and Grow strength, and further tiles are revealed through p.mineSeen in upgradeInGame, each with a NEW badge.

STORE SHAPE: single-currency rungs only (what costParts supports today). Power rungs past the first 1-2 are priced ONLY in the band material that opens them. Rungs are chunky (Water +12 a rung). The Ore yield and Water pockets tracks are cut, with an exact refund under a flag, written in the same save.
CAP HEAT TOLERANCE so the x4 zone always exists: at most +36 m (retention) to +56 m (craft). The HUD always quotes the price, and the band beat says 'digs now cost 4'.

ECONOMY METHOD (economy + craft): commit the career model; make career and journey bots read MINE_UPGRADE_IDS from the page and aim with their full reach; apply the tuning rule (price about 1-2 runs of income at that leg; each leg reachable at 70% or less of supply with the expected kit). Gates: 0 dead store visits in runs 1-10; no material balance above 3x its remaining demand; 85-90% of the store bought at the Promised Land and 100% no earlier than the last leg.

RICH SEAMS: 1 in 4 deep seams pays x3 and is drawn larger and tinted by material. It is hash-derived outside the chunk rng stream. It is the one variable reward and the target of the compass's third rung. Fix the stampFood retag at 22123 first.

DECISIVE COUNTERS: one flask kills every attached worm and every worm within about 160 units of any strand. Breeding is capped at 6-8 attached worms. One enzyme dose excises the whole connected infected component nearest the tap plus a one-segment margin, and commits on a TAP. A miss costs nothing. A save's first infection gets a 30 s clock.
READABLE MOULD: a mine-only cloud moveSpeed cut so that contact takes at least 6 s from first sight, measured by a probe. Avoiding a cloud becomes a skill.

DIG INTEGRITY: growDirected's fall-through is limited to tips near the pressed strand, which closes the 8x heat bypass. The mine gets its own node cap of 9000 and a 'full' ending. Digs are gated on sub._rockSolidified.

DEAD-DIG REFUND (craft): a dig that occupies no new cell and claims nothing is refunded, with the toast 'Nothing new that way - try another strand'. After 2 such digs, the 2-3 best frontier strands glow for about 3 s (craft and retention). This fixes the naive player's 28 m median.

FIRST VISIT SKIPS THE TITLE (retention): the gate tap goes straight into leg 1, run 1, with 2.5 s or less from tap to the first accepted dig. The gate reads 'Tap to dig' on a coarse pointer. Add a #minehint element of the mine's own, a canvas ghost-finger drag until the first dig, tap-to-dig-down on a strand, and one-shot tips in p.mineTips, each logged as a 'tutorial' event.

END SCREEN (retention/economy): the wordmark fits the width; rows count up by source (Reach, Seams, Island); ONE next-goal card with an inline Buy; Descend is the primary button (one tap to the next run) and Store is secondary. Materials are named in full, and the P icon is 0.95em.

RECORDS IN THE WORLD: best-depth and farthest-east dashed lines per leg, each firing a single NEW BEST beat when crossed. In a later milestone, the last attempt's fossil, capped at 300-400 quantised points.

JUICE: floaters spawned at the seam or pocket in the material's tint; synthesized Web Audio cues, with the seam ping rising a semitone per consecutive seam in a run; spent pockets dimmed; a haptics toggle; micro-shake behind a Reduced motion setting. Every cue is counted in __sfx.counts so checks can assert it.

NEVER LOSE A HAUL: bank on pagehide or after 60 s hidden (economy). 'Save & exit' becomes 'Fruit & exit', which banks through mineEndRun (retention). 'End run' is routed through mineEndRun with its own copy. 'Replay tutorial' is hidden, or opens an overlay that leaves the run untouched.

PRECISION IS SOLD: without the island compass the only instruction is 'Island N is east', plus a 5 s east-edge chevron on the first run after it is named (retention). Distance comes with rung 2. No banner or title gives away the island's east distance or taproot depth.

COMPASS TARGETS come only from generated chunks, plus lazy look-ahead generation of 1 chunk per idle slot (retention/craft). Assert them as model values through a __game.mine.compass() hook, with an order-independence check.

ACID VIAL as a PASS-THROUGH (retention/economy): when armed, the next dig may cross at most 3 cells of rock and must end in open ground. It is pre-checked by sampling solidAtWorld. A refusal keeps the vial and the water. The collision mask is untouched, and the tunnel strand is drawn amber over the rock.

DAILY DIG on the free layout: a fixed standard kit so scores compare; the first run of the day pays (seams + half reach); a local best; a 'Copy result' share string. An online board is optional, used only after a successful probe, and fails silently.
NEW JOURNEY: new seeds, one stacking rule per journey and one tint per completed journey. Cosmetics appear only after the Promised Land.

MILESTONE ORDER (retention): M1 unblocks, makes the build ship-safe and makes the tests trustworthy (the navdive planner in mine-check, the boot-check Supabase stub, #mine and '' added to boot-check). M2 is the first minute, M3 the economy, M4 juice and records, M5 threats. M6 is journey legs 1-3 with taproots, then compasses, then legs 4-8 and the ending, then the daily and polish. Commit and push each item as it lands.
TELEMETRY: run_end carries ms and detail 'L<leg>:<cause>:e<east>' within the existing carriers; add 'tutorial', 'island' and 'daily' events and a mine column in analytics.
mustReject: Economy's rock walls from the surface down to trunkRow-3 at every chunk seam, with a forced-open trunk row. It is a reserved corridor in all but name (the owner rejected that twice), it draws a structural slab every 24 columns, it collapses the maze into one highway, and it is the heaviest generator change proposed.

Economy's climb back up the island head to the surface. A dig is priced where it starts, so the climb taxes exactly the depth the late legs ask for (bare leg 8 costs 2,250 water), and it behaves like a return trip. The taproot target avoids it.

Economy's Heat VI, which moves the first line to 168 m. It deletes heat at the finale, which is the breaker's own defect ('+150 m deletes heat from a 168 m shaft'). Cap tolerance so the x4 zone always exists.

Economy's band-scaled pockets (10/15/20/25) as a premise change. It rests on a model, not a phase-1 finding, and 'numbers here are the owner's'. Keep +10 and revisit only if telemetry or bots show that deep pockets are ignored.
Economy's eager generation of the whole leg span at Descend (about 14 chunks, a long task of up to 600 ms, about 9k sprites). It is a phone perf and memory risk; generate lazily in idle time instead.
Craft's multi-part P+material prices (rewriting costParts across 5 call sites). Tiles like '110+10A' are harder to read on a phone and gate every rung twice. Keep single-currency rungs.

Craft's acid that dissolves rock by editing _fineSolid and _coarseCover and re-applying holes after every restamp. It fights the append-only mask; the pass-through strand gives the same play at lower risk.
Craft's 10-leg, 70-90 run Journey 1, with late legs targeting 6-15 retries of one fixed map. That is grind for portal players; cap it at 8 legs and no more than about 10 runs per leg.
Craft's single 'To the store' button on the end screen. It adds a tap to every run; Descend should be primary, with an inline Buy.

Any banner or title that gives the island's exact distance or depth for free (craft's '170 m east, 50 m down'; economy's 'the island is 96 m east, the way runs near 75 m'). It breaks the premise that the island compass sells precision.

Retention's SURFACE island as the leg's goal. With the crust measured at 5-7% solid, legs 1-4 become a drag-right crawl in which depth does not matter to the goal, and the dive run and the east run split into two half-games.
Retention's offline island fruiting. It is idle income in a skill game, a system with no decision in it, it rewards absence and it adds unearned P.

Retention's daily streak worth +3 P a day, and a daily played on the player's own loadout. It is a login reward in disguise: breaking the streak feels like a loss and the daily becomes a P farm. Scores on personal loadouts also cannot be compared. Use a fixed kit with the first run paid.
Retention's colony-colour shelf revealed at leg 5. It clutters the store mid-journey and competes with power rungs; cosmetics belong after the ending.
Retention's 'verify and fix rot creep' item. Once one dose excises the whole connected component, creep decides nothing, and touching the shared infectNetwork tuning risks the campaign mould checks.

Any teeth on the infection: forfeiting part of the haul, freezing digs, or a per-dig cooldown. They break the full-payout premise and the real-time feel. (All three proposals already reject this; the final design must keep it out.)
Missions, achievements, pick-before-descent modifiers and mid-run resume. Deferred or cut, as all three proposals agree: they add goal systems, drafting or 'Old', against the owner's rules.
verdict:
None of the three should be built as written. Build retention's milestone order and player-facing spec, with craft's journey structure and economy's economic method.

**From retention:** keep M1-M5 almost as specified. Every run ends and the build ships. The first minute teaches itself: the first visit skips the title, a ghost finger shows the drag, a tap digs down, and #minehint is visible on phones. Then come the payout and store reveal, the juice and records, and threats with counters that actually work. Retention's acceptance tests are the most concrete and the most checkable of the three.

**From craft, for the journey:** replace retention's surface island with a taproot at depth under the east island. Economy's measurement shows the crust is 5-7% solid, so a surface goal turns legs 1-4 into a drag-right crawl. The taproot makes every run use both axes and gives the compass one point to name. Reach it without corridors: curate the seeds offline and change the generator only in the island chunk. Do not use lateral repair in every chunk (retention) or walls plus a trunk row (economy).

**From economy, for the numbers:**
- Reach payout of 1 P per 5 m down or east, from running maxima, never less than 5 P.
- Water I priced at exactly that 5 P minimum, so run 1 always buys.
- A committed career model and the tuning rule.
- Rich seams (1 in 4).
- Banking on pagehide.
- A FRUIT NOW pill that shows what will bank.

**Everywhere else:**
- Rungs cost one currency each.
- Heat tolerance is capped so heat never disappears.
- One enzyme dose cuts the whole rot component, and a dig that gains no new ground is refunded.
- 8 legs: first island by run 3-5, Promised Land in about 35-60 runs.

**What gets cut:** offline income, the paid daily streak, colours mid-journey, multi-part prices, mask-editing acid, eager generation of the whole leg, heat that disappears at the finale, band-scaled pockets, and free coordinates that undercut the compass.

**Two owner decisions to raise explicitly:**
1. The affordability amendment, which fixes the soft lock seen in 36% of runs. Every proposal changes this; retention alone does not label it a premise change.
2. The taproot as the reading of "reach one, resurface and spore".

**Priorities:** M1-M3 give the most player value per unit of risk and should ship even if the journey slips. The generator work is the risk, so it waits until the test suite can be trusted (the navdive planner replaces the deepest-tip probe).

scores.strengths: The best player-facing layer of the three. Its first five minutes are designed second by second: the first visit skips the title, #minehint is its own element, a canvas ghost finger shows the drag, a tap on a strand digs down, and one-shot tips are logged as 'tutorial' events. The dead-end nudge makes the two most open tips glow on runs 1-5. Juice is complete and verifiable: floaters at the site, synthesized cues counted in __sfx.counts, and drained pocket art. Best-depth and farthest-east lines are drawn in the world, and the fossil is capped at 300 points. The end screen carries the next-goal card with an inline Buy. Its milestones are the finest-grained and easiest for one agent at a time to verify: economy (M3) is separate from threat counters (M5), and each has concrete bot and probe acceptance. It keeps single-currency rungs, so costParts is unchanged, which is the lowest store risk. The banded reach payout [6,4,3,2] makes deep metres worth more, which fits the heat ladder. The flask fix (killHits 1 and range 200 on the cfg clone), the slower clouds, the attached-worm breeding cap, the full refund-and-reset migration, and the 'free' layout pinned for mine-check are all correct and cheap. The rock-through is a pass-through with no mask edit, which is the safe way to build it.
scores.weaknesses: The journey sits on the open crust. Rock sprites are refused above surfaceY+0.5 cells (rock placement ~22219), so row 0 is about 5-7% solid, and the row-3 gallery is a second shallow road. Islands on the SURFACE can therefore be reached by 2-water crawls with no heat and no threats: leg 1 is about 30 digs from an 84 tank, and legs 1-4 never need depth. The two axes split into separate 'dive runs' and 'east runs'. East runs pay depth-only reach (11-19 P), so the journey axis is underpaid and dull. Its navdive-east acceptance (<=110 water) would pass without testing that depth is required. The payout also grows by accretion: first-descent floor, core bonus, streak bonus, richness, offline island income and a colours shelf, which works against 'few systems'. The Daily Dig runs on the player's own loadout, so scores are not comparable and it can be farmed. startWater stays at 84, which is 42 digs, over the 45-60 s premise at human pace. Its economy totals (about 2,700 P) are asserted, not modelled. Its M1 acceptance '0 living nodes inside _fineSolid' will conflict with its own vial later. Its M1 test items (navigator in mine-check, boot stub, 0/0 = broken, the box-in record) already landed in e6cf455 and ce89c7c.

scores.strengths: The clearest discipline: an explicit five-system budget in which every wrapper reuses those systems. It has the best leg goal: a TAPROOT chamber under the island at the leg's depth. That is a point target the island compass can name through rock. It avoids pricing a climb back to the surface (price is set at the source, so climbing 90 m costs about 76 water), and the celebration's filaments still 'resurface' the colony. It also has the best way to verify a leg. Journey-1 seeds are curated offline by a legprobe: the flood must reach the taproot, the path must be 1.3-2.0x the straight line, and bot runs-to-complete must be near target. That buys determinism and winnability without new generator repair code. Leg depth escalates (22 -> 158 m), so the journey walks the player down through the bands. The enzyme cuts the whole connected infected component, so one dose cures one breach whatever its size, and _removeNodes already orphans safely (16943). It orders tests first. It puts perf work (cached extents, pocket tests only near new growth) in the long-legs milestone instead of deferring it. The Daily Dig uses a fixed kit. Compasses only search generated chunks.
scores.weaknesses: Most of each leg's east distance is still the open crust at 2 a dig, followed by a plain dive at the island, so 'go down to afford going right' is only half built. The reach payout counts east distance on that open crust, which makes a farm. It moves to multi-part P+material prices: costParts becomes a list, touching buyUpgrade, the tiles, the sell path and store-check (124 assertions) for no design gain over single-currency rungs. Its rock-through (mineDissolve) edits _fineSolid, _coarseCover and cell.rock and re-applies holes after every restamp. That fights the append-only incremental stamp path the architect flagged, and it is the riskiest way to build the vial. The dead-end refund ('a dig that occupies no new cell') does not catch the measured problem, which is sideways digs that do take new cells but gain no depth, and it adds a cell-counting path to mineGrow. Ten legs, 70-90 runs and 3-5 h to the first ending is long for a portal audience. M2 bundles the store rewrite, startWater 84->64, richness, all the threat counters and the migration in one milestone, which is hard to verify one step at a time. New Journey hash seeds get no reachability gate. Its economy (about 6,000 P against 4,950 of demand) is asserted, not modelled.

scores.strengths: The only proposal that measured the crust highway (82 water crawls 168 m east at 0-5 m) and designed around it. In journey worlds it walls the seams above a per-leg TRUNK gallery row (the rows 3+18k the generator already uses). The trunk descends leg by leg, so going east really does mean going down, and threats, heat and materials join the journey rather than sitting beside it. The journey passes run on a separate rng stream (mineChunkRng(seed^K, ci)), so free-layout seeds and pins do not move. Its acceptance tests the structure directly: a flood restricted above the trunk never crosses the seam, and an east probe capped at 30 m depth cannot pass 27 m east. It has the only real economy model: measured route costs per band, careers modelled across human-overhead rows (26-40 runs, all 40/40 finishing), a tuning rule ('reachable at <=70% of supply'), and a plan to commit the model. Run 1 buys by construction (a minimum payout of 5 P against a Water I price of 5 P). Rungs are single-currency, and each band's material buys the next leg's key rung. It has the best soft-lock rule: the working front, meaning the cheapest clean strand within one resting-view height of the focus, then the existing 1.6 s grace, then a visible countdown, cancelled by any dig or any water gained. The FRUIT NOW pill shows what it will bank. It prices the dig at the parent that actually grew. Pagehide banking protects the haul. The per-leg banner is a cheap legibility win.
scores.weaknesses: Heat VI moves the first line to 168 m, and tolerance shifts the whole ladder (mineGrowCost 22620), so it deletes heat from the entire shaft, the exact defect the breaker reported. It was only needed because landfall climbs the island head back to the surface ('down + east + up'), which is priced at the deep source. Its gate rule ('a leg must NOT be reachable without its key heat rung') is a hard wall, and its own v1 stranded careers for 380 dead runs. The seam walls plus the forced-open trunk repair are the riskiest generator change in any proposal. The trunk broke on 2 of 3 seeds below 45 m before repair, and the walls must be reviewed so they do not read as a painted barrier or a reserved corridor. Closing row 0 also means letting seam plugs reach past surfaceY+0.5 cells; drawLevelRocks clips at the surface, so this is fine. Eager generation of the whole leg span at Descend (about 14 chunks and 9k sprites, about 30 ms a chunk, every threat live, all of it to be fine-stamped) is a long-task and memory risk the compasses do not need. It misses the cloud-speed fix: avoidance fails today because clouds lunge in 1.6 s. Pockets paying by band is a premise change that its own heat chain undercuts, since trunk digs cost 2 once the key rung is bought. Journey 1 at about 1 h is short for 'max time'. Its human-overhead factors are assumptions until telemetry exists.

spec.pitch:
THE DEEP MINE. You grow a glowing fungal colony through a rock maze on one tank of water, and every dig costs more the deeper it starts: 2 water, then 4 / 8 / 16 past 42 / 84 / 126 m. Somewhere to the east and below lies the root of a green island. Reach it and the colony takes root there and the next, harder world begins; there are eight islands between you and the Promised Land. When the tank runs dry the colony spores and pays for every metre it reached and every seam it dug. You buy one thing that makes the next run visibly better: a bigger tank, a longer dig, a tool that ends a threat outright, or a compass that points through rock.

LOOP IN ONE LINE: dig down and east until dry -> the colony spores and pays for every metre -> buy one thing -> descend again and get farther.
spec.coreLoop:
FIVE SYSTEMS, EACH DEEP, AND NOTHING ELSE
1. The dig and its water price (the heat staircase).
2. The maze, with every reward off the route.
3. Two threats, each with one bought counter that fully answers it.
4. The journey: eight fixed legs, each ending at an island's root.
5. The store: power, kit and knowledge (compasses).
Every wrapper (reach payout, records, fossil, Daily Dig, New Journey) reuses these five and adds no rule of its own. There are no cards, no drafting and no per-run picks.

A DIG (1.5-2 s at a human pace)
- Press any living strand and drag. The arrow shows the reach (153 world units at grow 2, 459 at grow 6) and, at its head, the price where you pressed (2/4/8/16).
- Release: the strands reveal over about a second with the grow sound, and the tank drops by that price.
- A tap on a strand digs straight down from it.
- Every seam or pocket the new tissue claims pays on the spot, with a floater and a sound at the site. Every 5 m of new depth pops '+1 P' at the tip.
- Each dig is a routing decision: which strand, which corridor, and whether a seam (+3 P, or +2/+6 of a deep material) or a pocket (+10 water, once) is worth the detour. You also route to stay out of the green sensing washes.

A RUN
Length: run 1 is 30-35 digs (45-65 s); legs 3-5 are 60-80 digs (1.5-2.5 min); legs 6-8 are 80-110 digs (2.5-4 min).
- It opens with the leg banner ('LEG 3 · DRY GROUND · no water pockets above 42 m'). On a leg's first run a 5 s chevron at the east edge reads 'Island 3 is east'.
- You dig down from the west hill. On leg 1 the shallow galleries carry you east.
- From leg 2 the shallow road breaks: most of its gallery seams are sealed. The cheap way east runs through 42-84 m (84-126 m from leg 7), where the worms, mould, heat and deep materials are.
- The goal is the island's TAPROOT: a glowing knot in a chamber beneath the green island hill. It is deeper on every leg: 24 m on leg 1, 140 m on leg 8.
- On the way you detour for seams and pockets, flask the worms that latch on, cut out the rot before its clock ends, and spend a vial on the one wall worth eating.
- The run ends when you reach the taproot (ROOTED: a bonus and the next leg), or when:
  - the tank cannot pay where you are working (FRUIT NOW, automatic after 6 s),
  - the rot clock runs out,
  - the node cap is reached, or
  - you end it from the menu.
- Every ending pays in full.

BETWEEN RUNS (1-2 taps)
The end screen counts the payout up by source, names one next goal with an inline Buy, and offers [Descend] as the primary button. The full store is one tap away.

A SESSION (5-15 min, 3-8 runs)
- In runs 1-10 almost every store visit buys something.
- Every session holds a 'first': a new band, a new threat and its tile, a new store tile, a leg's rule, an island in sight, or a landfall.
- It ends on a named near goal ('Island 4: your farthest is 26 m short', 'Grow strength IV: 24 Garnet, you have 9, found at 84-126 m').

THE JOURNEY (Journey I: 8 legs, 35-50 runs, 70-110 min)
- Each leg is one fixed world, so a retry is mastery.
- Your best depth and farthest east are dashed lines in the world, and your last attempt's colony shows as a dim fossil.
- The first island falls on run 3-5.
- The Promised Land ends Journey I with a finale and credits.

THE LONG TAIL
- The Daily Dig: a shared seed, a fixed kit, one paid run a day, deepest wins.
- New Journeys II-VIII: new seeds, one stacking rule each, and the store is kept.
- Strains (strand colours) as the P sink after the ending.
- Per-leg records.
spec.journey:
STRUCTURE
- A journey is 8 legs. A leg is one 504 x 168 world of 21 chunks, each 24 columns (unchanged).
- The hill is at chunk 1 (root column 36, the WEST). The island is at chunk 1+E (the EAST): 12 columns of green surface drawn with the existing goalhill/goalbush/tree art. drawMineHill/mineHillSpan (40096-40113) take a list of hills.
- On leg 2+ the west hill is the previous island (same art).
- Beneath the island hangs its TAPROOT:
  - a canvas-drawn, pulsing mint knot in a carved chamber of radius 2.5 cells, at (hill + east metres, depth metres);
  - a few short filaments hang from the island hill and fade out within about 6 m, so the island reads as rooted without giving away the depth.
- LANDFALL: any clean strand within 1.5 cells (54 units) of the knot's centre.
  - The run ends that frame with cause 'island'.
  - The filaments light up from the taproot to the island hill, which fruits (startCelebration 33442 with an 'island' side, via hillRiseAtX 33429).
  - The colony resurfaces and spores on the island in the celebration, never by a priced climb.
  - The next Descend starts leg N+1 from that island.
- Failing leaves you on the same leg, with the same world.

SEEDS
- Journey I uses 8 curated seeds (CONFIG.mine.journey.legs[n].seed, i.e. seeded by journey and leg index).
- tests/bots/legprobe.cjs picks each one offline from 50 candidates. The seed must pass all three tests:
  - the fine-mask flood from the home head reaches the taproot;
  - the shortest path is 1.3-2.0x the straight line;
  - the cheapest-water route meets the leg's depth share.
- Journeys II-IV get their own curated tables; V+ cycle them. A seed is identical for every player and every retry.

TWO LAYOUTS
- 'journey' is the legs (#leg,<j>,<l> for tools).
- 'free' is today's centre-hill descent, byte-identical. It serves #mine,<seed>, the Daily Dig and the 190 existing mine-check pins.

GOING RIGHT MEANS GOING DOWN (journey layout only)
Measured: rock sprites are refused above surfaceY + 0.5 cell (22219, 22260). The top of row 0 is therefore 5-7% solid, and a colony crawls 168 m east for 82 water at 0-5 m. With that crust open, a surface goal would never require going down. Three changes fix it:
(a) THE CRUST CLOSES. In journey worlds a sprite may reach the surface (the clamp becomes surfaceY + 0.05 cell; drawLevelRocks already clips at the surface).
(b) THE SHALLOW ROAD BREAKS. The existing gallery seal draw (21703, rng() < sealCh, drawn unconditionally) compares against a per-band chance from the leg row (sealByBand) instead of the single 0.12.
  - A sealed seam is the rock the maze already uses. No row is reserved, forced open or painted.
  - Where a shallow crossing survives, it is a shortcut a returning player learns.
(c) ONLY THE ISLAND CHUNK gets new carving:
  - the taproot chamber;
  - the flood-and-repair generalized from 21995-22064: flood from the chamber, and if no gallery cell on either seam is reached, open the shortest radius-1.7 connectors;
  - all on its own hash rng, mineChunkRng(seed ^ 0x7A9, ci), after every existing draw.
All three are journey-only, and the free layout's chunk stats are asserted byte-identical.

LEG TABLE (CONFIG.mine.journey.legs; M14 calibrates E and the depths)
Columns: leg | name | E (chunks) / taproot east | taproot depth | crossing band (sealByBand for 0-42 / 42-84 / 84-126 m) | the leg's one rule | island bonus | expected kit on arrival | target runs
| 1 | First Light | 4 / 96 m | 24 m | 0-42 m (0.12 / 0.12 / 0.12) | none: threat-free | 20 | Water 1-2, Grow 1-2 | 2-4 |
| 2 | The Coal Road | 6 / 144 m | 58 m | 42-84 m (0.55 / 0.12 / 0.12) | worms from 42 m, as standard | 30 | Water 3, Grow 2, Heat 1, Flask 1 | 3-6 |
| 3 | Dry Ground | 8 / 192 m | 72 m | 42-84 m (0.70 / 0.12 / 0.12) | no water pockets above 42 m | 40 | Water 4, Grow 3, Heat 2 | 3-6 |
| 4 | Mould Country | 9 / 216 m | 92 m | 42-84 m (0.70 / 0.12 / 0.12) | mould also at 42-84 m (1 cloud per chunk) | 50 | Water 5, Grow 3, Heat 3, Enzyme 1 | 3-6 |
| 5 | Rich Veins | 11 / 264 m | 104 m | 42-84 m (0.75 / 0.20 / 0.12) | 1 deep seam in 2 is rich | 60 | Water 6, Grow 4, Heat 4 | 3-6 |
| 6 | Hot Rock | 10 / 240 m | 112 m | 42-84 m (0.75 / 0.20 / 0.12) | price lines 6 m shallower (safeDepth 36) | 70 | Water 6, Grow 4, Heat 4, Enzyme 2 | 3-6 |
| 7 | The Swarm | 13 / 312 m | 126 m | 84-126 m (0.75 / 0.60 / 0.12) | worms x2 below 42 m | 85 | Water 7, Flask 2-3, Enzyme 2 | 4-7 |
| 8 | The Promised Land | 15 / 360 m (island chunk 16) | 140 m | 84-126 m (0.75 / 0.65 / 0.12) | +1 worm and +1 cloud per chunk below 84 m; a double-width island | 150 | the full kit | 4-7 |

ESCALATION RULES
- Band 0 (0-42 m) is threat-free on every leg, and nothing respawns.
- Rules are overrides on the cfg clone in configForLevel (32461-32493) and use existing knobs only: threatBands, reservoirsPerBand (made per band), richChance, heat.safeDepth and gallerySealChance (made per band).
- mineBeat, mineZoom and mineClampZoom read state.config (37244-37251, 37143, 37161).

CALIBRATION RULE
- With the expected arrival kit, the navigator must reach the taproot on at most 70% of supply (start water + half the route's pockets).
- With the bare kit it must need more than 100% (legs 3-8).
- A leg that takes more than 7 runs at the median gets its island pulled in one chunk. A leg under 3 runs gets it pushed out one chunk.

RECORDS PER LEG
- Best depth is a dashed horizontal line and farthest east a dashed vertical line, each labelled at the screen edge. Crossing either fires a one-shot NEW DEEPEST / NEW FARTHEST beat.
- The last failed attempt's colony shows as a dim fossil (M13).
- The title and end screen name the gap ('Island 4: your farthest is 26 m short').

THE ENDING
Landing on leg 8 plays, in order:
1. ROOTED.
2. The camera pulls back over the double-width island.
3. A canvas journey strip, on which all 8 islands burst spores 300 ms apart over a rising chord.
4. 'The Promised Land. Your colony spans the world.'
5. Credits (showCredits).
The title then gets a 'Journey I' badge, the Gold strain unlocks, and 'Begin Journey II' appears. Everything is banked before anything animates.

AFTER
New Journey J keeps the store and adds one stacking rule:
- II Hotter: price lines 10 m shallower.
- III Thirsty: start water -12.
- IV Hungry: worms x2, 0.3 water/s each.
- V Rotten: mould from 42 m, rot clock 15 s.
- VI Stingy: pockets +7.
- VII Far: every island +2 chunks, capped at chunk 19.
- VIII+: all of them.
Each completion unlocks a strain and records 'fewest runs to the Promised Land'. The Daily Dig runs alongside from the first landfall.
spec.economy:
CURRENCIES
- Phosphorus (P, p.minerals) is the general currency. Anthracite (42-84 m), Garnet (84-126 m) and Hematite (126-168 m) are held in p.mats. Whole numbers everywhere.
- The rule of the shelf: the first rungs of every track cost P. A power rung past its first two costs the material from the depth it opens, and its tile says where that material is found.

SOURCES (all banked by mineBank in presentMineEnd 33215, on every ending)
1. REACH (new, CONFIG.mine.reach):
   - 1 P per 5 m of the run's deepest clean depth, plus 1 P per 10 m of its farthest east of the hill (journey legs only). Never less than 5 P.
   - Both are running maxima kept in mineFrame, so rot never erases progress.
   - Depth: 42 m = 8, 84 m = 16, 126 m = 25, 168 m = 33. East: 96 m = 9, 192 m = 19, 360 m = 36.
   - It shows live in the HUD P count, with a '+1 P' pop at the tip.
   - Depth pays double per metre because depth is where the heat, the threats and the materials are.
2. PHOSPHORUS SEAMS: 3 P each, 0-42 m only, 2 per chunk (unchanged).
3. DEEP SEAMS: 2 of their band's material and no P (the recorded rule). 1 in 4 is RICH, pays 6 and is drawn 1.3x larger. Richness is a hash of seed, chunk and spot index, outside the chunk rng. Leg 5 makes it 1 in 2.
4. ISLAND BONUS, on the first landfall of each leg: 20 / 30 / 40 / 50 / 60 / 70 / 85 / 150.
5. DAILY DIG: its one paid run a day pays seams + half the reach, so it is never the best farm.
WATER is fuel, not money: start 60 (+12 a rung); pockets give +10 once each, 1 per band per chunk.

THE SHELF
36 rungs, one currency per rung, so costParts (14313) and buyUpgrade (14323) are unchanged. When each track is revealed is in brackets.
- WATER TANK, +12 start water (60 -> 156): 5 P, 12 P, 25 P, 45 P, 80 P, 30 Anthracite, 24 Garnet, 16 Hematite. [visit 1]
- GROW STRENGTH, +1 step (2 -> 6; reach 153 -> 459 units): 12 P, 35 P, 20 Anthracite, 24 Garnet. [visit 1]
- HEAT TOLERANCE, first price line 14 m deeper a rung (42 -> 98 m; the lines end at 98 / 140, so x4 and x8 always exist): 15 P, 14 Anthracite, 24 Anthracite, 20 Garnet. [first strand past 42 m]
- MUCUS FLASKS, carry 1 / 2 / 3: 10 P, 40 P, 14 Anthracite. [first worm attach, or leg 2]
- CUTTING ENZYME, carry 1 / 2 / 3: 15 P, 50 P, 14 Garnet. [first cloud on screen, or leg 4]
- OXALIC VIAL, carry 1 / 2 / 3: 50 P, 12 Garnet, 12 Hematite. [leg 3]
- ISLAND COMPASS: bearing 12 P; + distance 40 P. [visit 2 on a journey save]
- ANTHRACITE COMPASS: bearing 20 P; + distance 60 P; richest within 90 m 12 Anthracite. [first anthracite seam]
- GARNET COMPASS: 40 P; 100 P; 12 Garnet. [first garnet seam]
- HEMATITE COMPASS: 60 P; 140 P; 12 Hematite. [first hematite seam]
- STRAINS (cosmetic strand tints), only after the Promised Land: Amber 150, Violet 250, Ghost 400, Coal 600 P, plus one unique strain per completed journey.
TOTALS: 866 P + 114 Anthracite + 106 Garnet + 40 Hematite. The old shelf was 3,237 P + 18 / 31 / 13.

WHERE EACH MATERIAL GOES
- Anthracite (legs 2-6 cross its band): Water VI, Grow III, Heat II-III, Flask III, the Anthracite compass III.
- Garnet (legs 7-8 cross its band, the leg 4-6 taproots sit in it, and dives reach it): Water VII, Grow IV, Heat IV, Enzyme III, Vial II, the Garnet compass III.
- Hematite (taproot dives on legs 7-8, and deliberate dives): Water VIII, Vial III, the Hematite compass III. These are the last rungs of the journey.

CUT, WITH AN EXACT REFUND
- Ore yield (the dominant buy, and it silently multiplied deep materials by 4) and Water pockets (the weakest value on the shelf) are cut.
- migrateProgress (13719), flag migratedMineShelfV2:
  - refund every mine rung ever bought, at its OLD price, into p.minerals and p.mats;
  - clear p.mineUpgrades, in the same save;
  - toast 'The store was restocked — your Phosphorus is back'.
- Heat tolerance's 25 m step becomes 14 m, over 4 rungs. The old 6 x 25 m deleted heat from the shaft.

PAYOUT PER RUN (model median, excluding island bonuses)
| stage | P per run | materials per run |
|---|---|---|
| Run 1 | 12-13 | - |
| Leg 1 | 17 | - |
| Leg 2 | 18 | +4 A |
| Leg 3 | 30 | +12 A |
| Leg 4 | 34 | +15 A |
| Leg 5 | 40 | +22 A |
| Leg 6 | 43 | +24 A |
| Leg 7 | 45 | +15 G |
| Leg 8 | 53 | +19 G |
Dives, about a quarter of runs on legs 3-7, pay 25-40 P plus 12-18 of the target material.

PACE
- Run 1 always buys Water I: the minimum payout is 5, and so is its price.
- Runs 1-10: 1.3-1.5 purchases a visit, with at most 1 visit that buys nothing.
- Legs 3-4: 1.5-1.8 purchases a visit.
- Legs 5-7: 0.2-1.0 a visit (material rungs, dives).
- Leg 8: the last 1-3 rungs; the final runs are pure journey.

WHEN THE STORE RUNS OUT
- P rungs are exhausted by legs 5-6. Material rungs last through leg 8.
- The model has 97% of rungs bought at the final landfall, with the last Hematite rungs 1-3 runs before it.
- Surplus P (about 600 in the model) and New Journey income fund the strains. After that, P is a lifetime stat by design.
spec.runEnding:
HOW EVERY RUN ENDS
Every ending goes mineEndRun(state, cause) (22714) -> presentRunOver -> presentMineEnd (33215) -> mineBank(r), which is idempotent. All endings are died:false and all pay IN FULL: reach + seams + materials + any island bonus. The depth paid and recorded is state.mineMaxDepth, the running maximum of clean depth kept in mineFrame. An infected ending no longer shows 99 m after reaching 107.

THE CAUSES
1. 'dry', with two triggers.
   (a) As today: water below the cheapest dig anywhere (mineCheapestCost 22686) for OUT_OF_FUEL_GRACE_MS (1.6 s). A pocket the last dig is about to reach still pays first.
   (b) THE SOFT-LOCK FIX (mineStuckCheck, beside mineFuelCheck 22703): water is below costHere, the price at the focus strand (mineDigCost 22678 at state._mineFocus, else the deepest clean tip). That is the number the chip shows.
   - A 6 s countdown (CONFIG.mine.stuckFruitMs) runs only while no reveal is in flight, no menu is open and no pointer is held.
   - Any successful dig, and any water gained, resets it.
   - At zero the run ends.
   Copy: 'Out of water at 92 m. The colony fruits and spores.'
2. 'fruit'. Whenever water < costHere, the price chip becomes the FRUIT NOW pill ('FRUIT NOW · +23 P', the bankable total, with the countdown as a conic ring). One tap ends the run.
   Copy: 'You called it at 92 m. Every spore is yours.'
   A refused dig toasts 'Not enough water — a dig here costs 8. Fruit now to bank +23 P.'
3. 'infected'. The rot clock (20 s; 30 s on a save's first infection) reaches zero. The whole colony turns green, fruits and pays.
   Copy: 'The rot took the colony at 92 m. What it spored is yours.'
4. 'abandon'. Settings > 'End descent (banks everything)' replaces 'End run', and forceFruitAbandon (33063) is routed through mineEndRun in the mine.
   Copy: 'You ended the descent at 92 m. Everything dug is banked.'
5. 'quit'. Settings > 'Exit to title (banks everything)' replaces 'Save & exit', which deleted the haul (onSaveExit 35976). It banks through mineBank and shows the title with the toast '+23 P banked'. 'Replay tutorial' is hidden in the mine, because it restarted the run.
6. 'island'. Landfall on the taproot. The wordmark is ROOTED and the island bonus is added.
   Copy: 'Your colony took root on Island 2. Leg 3, Dry Ground, starts there.'
7. 'promised'. Landfall on leg 8: the finale.
8. 'full'. The node cap is reached (mine maxNodes 9000 in configForLevel, instead of the shared 6000 at 2718). The run ends instead of refusing every dig as 'Solid rock'.
   Copy: 'The colony fills every passage it can reach, and fruits.'

CLOSING THE TAB NEVER LOSES A HAUL
On visibilitychange -> hidden and on pagehide, the would-be payout is written to p.minePending. Coming back to the tab clears it. The next boot banks a leftover once, and the title says 'Your last descent spored +23 P'.

WHY THIS SOFT-LOCK RULE
- mineFuelCheck asks whether the SHALLOWEST strand is affordable (always 2), while the working front costs 4-16.
- That left 14 of 39 bot runs and 5 of 12 playtest runs live and idle for 30-60 s.
- The fix keeps the recovery play the old rule was written for: a cheap dig resets the countdown and moves the focus.
- It bounds dead time at 6 s, and the pill makes the ending one obvious tap that says what it banks.

INFECTION
- One clock per colony, derived from 'is anything infected' (mineInfectionCheck 22582). It stops only when every infected strand is gone.
- Infected strands cannot be grown from.
- A top banner reads 'ROT 14 s — tap the enzyme, then the rot', or 'ROT 14 s — the colony will fruit' with an empty bag.
- Full payout: this is the interlock with the bought enzyme.
spec.threatsAndCounters:
WORMS (42 m and below)
Placement: per chunk from threatBands, 1 per chunk at 42-84 and 84-126 m and 2 at 126-168 m, times the leg rule. Nothing respawns. Sight is 300 units.
- An attached worm drains 0.2 water/s (1 every 5 s, through mineDrainDebt, so the tank stays whole).
- It breeds at 5%/s while feeding, but only while fewer than 6 worms are attached. This lives in the stepNematodes mine branch (17598-17760). The world cap of 16, which silently stopped breeding once 4 chunks existed, is raised to a safety bound of 64.
- Unanswered, it costs about 3 worms and about 20 water by 40 s, and at the cap 6 worms drain 1.2 water/s. That is a real but recoverable pressure.
- READABLE:
  - Attached worms are drawn at 2.5x with a 1 Hz pulsing ring on the host strand (drawNematodes 40150).
  - An off-screen attached worm gets a worm-coloured chevron at the screen edge.
  - The HUD chip reads '3 · -0.6/s', and tapping it pans to the nearest attached worm.
  - The first attach shows a one-time tip.
  - The green flat sensing wash is unchanged. The attach ring is a separate mark.

MUCUS FLASK (bought, carry 1-3, restocked every descent)
- One tap kills every worm attached to, or within 160 units of, any clean strand. Mine-only overrides on the cfg clone: nematodes.killHits 3 -> 1, actions.excrete.range 80 -> 160.
- The drain reads 0/s on the next tick.
- A burst with no worm in range costs nothing.
- Copy: 'Mucus burst — 3 worms killed.'
- DECISIVE: the threat is a visible rate, one tap sets it to zero, and nothing respawns. The decision is timing: throw now and kill one, or later and kill the brood.

MOULD (84 m and below; also 42-84 m on Mould Country)
One cloud per chunk. The flat green wash is unchanged.
- Mine-only overrides sit beside the campaign machinery (CONFIG.mine.trych onto cfg.trichoderma, 32476-32478):
  - moveSpeed 2.5 -> 0.5 cells a tick. A cloud that senses you at the edge of its ring needs at least 6 s to arrive; today it lunges in 1.6 s.
  - firstTouchRings 12 -> 6, so a breach is about 10-25 strands, not 41-55.
- Clouds still eat the seams they see, so a race for a garnet seam stays in the game.
- Contact starts ONE colony clock: 20 s, or 30 s on a save's first infection. Two breaches need two cures.
- Rot creep is left as tuned.

CUTTING ENZYME (bought, carry 1-3)
- Arm it, then TAP (or drag) near the rot.
- In the mine, mineUseAmputate (22563) removes:
  - the whole connected infected component nearest the tap, within 300 units, found by walking parent/child links between infected nodes;
  - plus the clean nodes within one segment of it.
  It works through net._removeNodes (16943) and clears the cloud cells there.
- Orphaned clean tissue keeps living.
- With no rot within 300 units it refuses and the dose is kept.
- One dose cures one breach, however far it has spread. Today one dose left 12 of 55 strands rotten, and three doses cost 32% of the colony.
- Copy: 'Cut out 14 rotten strands — the colony is clean.'
- DECISIVE: the clock is on screen and one aimed tap stops it.

OXALIC VIAL (the owner-sanctioned rock-through consumable; bought, carry 1-3, from leg 3)
- Tap the vial: the aim arrow turns acid-yellow and outlines the rock it would cross.
- The next dig may pass through up to 108 units (3 cells) of rock and must come out in open ground. growDirected gets a rockBudget option, honoured only when sub.mine is set and a vial is armed.
- It is pre-checked by sampling solidAtWorld along the aim before anything is charged. If the rock is too thick, the toast reads 'Too thick for the acid' and the vial and water are kept.
- The collision mask is NOT edited. The tunnel strands are flagged n.acid and drawn amber over the rock with an etched halo. Rock stays a wall for everything else.
- Uses:
  - the walled-in seams and pockets the generator already leaves as bait (2 of 24 seams and 1 of 12 pockets are stranded);
  - one wall on the way east.

HEAT (passive; priced, never enforced)
- 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 water past 42 / 84 / 126 m, priced at the pressed strand.
- The 8x bypass is closed: a dig can only fall through to a tip within 90 units on the same price step.
- Tolerance is 4 x 14 m, so the lines sit at 98 / 140 m at most, and 4 and 8 always exist below them.
- The chip always quotes the price, the aim arrow repeats it at its head, and the band beat says 'Digs now cost 4'.
spec.onboarding:
PRINCIPLE
Teach by doing, in the world, once. There are no modals, because the owner's data showed campaign onboarding polish did nothing. Every tip is one non-blocking line in #minehint or on the map, fires once per save (p.mineTips), and is logged as a 'tutorial' telemetry event with its id and time, so the funnel is measured rather than assumed.

THE FIRST 5 MINUTES

0:00 — The load gate reads 'Tap to dig' on a coarse pointer, 'Click to dig' otherwise (showLoading 31873). The tap starts audio.
- A FIRST VISIT (no p.mineBest, no runs) SKIPS THE TITLE: the tap goes straight into Leg 1, run 1 (enterGame 40423 -> beginMineRun), with no DIG word animation.
- The curtain lifts within 600 ms and input goes live on the reveal. Target: 2.5 s or less from the tap to the first accepted dig (6.9 s today).

0:01 — The root pulses under the hill.
- A canvas GHOST FINGER (a 14 px mint dot with a trailing arrow) slides 110 px down the most open ray from the root, every 1.6 s.
- #minehint, the mine's own element (the .hint rules at CSS 693/1011/1059 cannot hide it), sits top centre under the HUD: 'Drag down from the colony to dig'.
- A tap on the colony also digs straight down.
- Nothing else is on screen: no kit, and no second HUD row.

0:03 — Dig 1: the grow sound, and water 60 -> 58 with a '-2' tick.
- The hint becomes 'Every dig costs water — the deeper, the more' for 3 s.
- The ghost leaves. On runs 1-2 it comes back after 6 s without a dig.

0:05-0:15 — '+1 P' pops at the tip every 5 m of depth, with a soft tick, and the HUD P count rises. Depth pays.

0:10-0:25 — The first Phosphorus seam on screen gets a soft pulsing ring and 'Phosphorus — grow into it'. When it pays: a '+3 P' floater at the seam and a ping.

0:20-0:35 — The first pocket on screen gets 'Water pocket — touch it for +10'. When tapped: '+10 water', a glug, and the pocket art drains, so a spent pocket reads as spent.

About 0:35 — 6 m above the line, a label sits on it: 'Past 42 m every dig costs 4'.
- On crossing, the beat reads '42 m · ANTHRACITE' with the second line 'Digs now cost 4'.
- The soil turns black and the price chip pulses.

DEAD-END NUDGE (runs 1-5) — Two digs in a row that each add fewer than 2 new cells make the two tips with the most open ground ahead glow for 4 s, and the hint reads 'Dead end — dig from a glowing tip'. This is what fixes the naive always-dig-from-the-bottom player (median 28 m today).

0:45-1:00 — At 3 digs left or fewer the water chip turns amber and reads '3 left'. When the price here beats the tank, the chip becomes 'FRUIT NOW · +11 P' with its 6 s ring. The run ends on SPORED.

About 1:00 — The end screen:
- 'Your first descent';
- rows counting up: 'Depth 52 m +10', 'Phosphorus seams x2 +6';
- the next-goal card 'Water tank: start with 12 more water · 5 P [Buy]';
- [Descend].
Buying is one tap, and so is descending.

Run 2 (about 1:10) — The leg banner 'LEG 1 · FIRST LIGHT' and a 5 s east-edge chevron: 'Island 1 is east — its root lies under the green hill'. The first sight of the island hill brings 'Reach the island's root to move on'.

Runs 2-4 — Grow strength I (12 P).
- Landfall on island 1 comes on run 3 at the model median, about 4-5 minutes in.
- It brings the ROOTED celebration, +20 P, and 'Leg 2: The Coal Road' lighting up on the journey strip.
- The store gains a NEW tile, the Island compass.

Leg 2 — The first worm to attach brings 'A worm is drinking your water. Mucus flasks kill worms — in the store.', and the flask tile shows NEW.

Leg 4, or a deep dive — The first cloud on screen brings 'Mould: one touch starts a 30 s rot clock'. The first infection gets the 30 s clock and 'Rot! Arm the enzyme and tap the rot.' The enzyme tile shows NEW.

PROGRESSIVE STORE REVEAL
upgradeInGame (14249) reads p.mineSeen, and the shelf and the buy path share that one predicate.
- Visit 1: exactly two tiles, Water tank (5 P, highlighted) and Grow strength (12 P).
- + Heat tolerance: a strand first passes 42 m.
- + Mucus flasks: the first worm attaches, or leg 2 begins.
- + Island compass: store visit 2 on a journey save.
- + Cutting enzyme: the first cloud comes on screen, or leg 4 begins.
- + Each material compass: that material's first seam.
- + Oxalic vial: leg 3 begins.
- + Strains: only after the Promised Land.
A newly revealed tile carries a NEW badge for one visit and is the next-goal card's first pick. At most 5 tiles show before run 5.

NEXT-GOAL PRIORITY (the end-screen card)
new tile > grow > water > heat (if the leg's route runs past the line) > flask (if worms were met) > enzyme (if rot was met) > island compass > the compass for a material the next power rung needs > vial.
- If nothing is affordable, the card shows the nearest rung: '6 P short', or 'Grow strength IV: 24 Garnet, you have 9 (found at 84-126 m)'.
- If the store is done, it shows the leg gap: 'Island 5: your farthest is 26 m short'.
spec.feedbackAndJuice:
FLOATERS (M4)
mineOreRewards (22376) and mineWaterPickups (22418) return per-pile lists [{x, y, mat, n}]. addEnergyFloater and drawFloaters (38540/38612) take an icon, a colour and a size.
- '+1 P': 12 px lilac, at the deepest tip, per reach tick.
- '+3 P': 18 px lilac (#c9a2e8), at the seam.
- '+2 Anthracite' (#d8b36a), '+2 Hematite' (#d98a5a), and '+6 Garnet!' (#d8566a) for a rich seam.
- '+10 water': blue, at the pocket.
- '-3 worms': at a flask burst.
- 'Cut 14': at an enzyme cut.
They rise 40 px over 900 ms with an outline, at most 12 live at once.

STATE LEGIBILITY
- Tapped pockets are drawn at 35% alpha with a dry crack.
- Seams are tinted by material and scaled by richness (the same leaf-litter art).
- The water chip turns amber with 'N left' at 3 digs or fewer.
- The price chip pulses when the price changes, and becomes the FRUIT NOW pill.
- The rot banner, and the rings on attached worms.
- Kit buttons pulse while their threat is present.

SOUNDS
All synthesized with Web Audio in __m_render_sfx (24820), following the click() pattern:
- behind isSfxMuted;
- counted in window.__sfx.counts;
- at most 6 voices, peaking at -12 dBFS;
- the AudioContext resumes on the gate tap.
The seam ping and pocket glug land in M4; the rest in M12.

|---|---|
| dig | the existing playGrowBurst |
